title: Relative global complete intersections are flat
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$, and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Suppose $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

mathlib_searches.query: relative global complete intersection is flat ring map
mathlib_searches.results: RingHom.Flat, RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff, Algebra.Smooth.flat_of_isNoetherianRing; no complete-intersection flatness theorem

mathlib_searches.query: polynomial quotient with fibre dimension number of equations is flat
mathlib_searches.results: Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension and Algebra.Smooth.flat; these require smoothness/Jacobian hypotheses, not relative complete intersection
Only RingTheory/Extension/Presentation/Basic.lean:106 docstring mentions complete intersection; no syntomic or relative complete-intersection theorem.
